bib.title: To CoT or not to CoT? Chain-of-thought helps mainly on math and symbolic reasoning
bib.venue: ICLR 2025 (Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025; arXiv v3 7 May 2025)

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; Tables 7-16 (per-dataset numbers, unparseable rates, answer-span indices) skimmed, not transcribed.

question: For which kinds of tasks does prompt-based chain-of-thought actually improve over direct answering, and why?
hypothesis: Common belief (tested and rejected): CoT outperforms direct answering on nearly all reasoning problems; the authors expect gains mainly where symbolic execution is needed.
contributions: Meta-analysis of 110 papers / 1,218 comparisons showing CoT gains concentrate in math, symbolic and logic
Own evaluation of 20 datasets x 14 models, zero-shot and few-shot
MMLU analysis: gain concentrated on items containing '='
Plan vs execution decomposition showing tool solvers beat CoT on symbolic tasks

method.summary: Meta-analysis of CoT-vs-direct comparisons in ICLR/EACL/NAACL 2024 papers, plus own greedy-decoded zero/few-shot evaluations of 14 LLMs on 20 datasets, plus a plan/execute decomposition (direct, CoT, tool solver) on GSM8K, GSM8K-Hard, ContextHub, FOLIO.
method.task: Comparing CoT vs direct-answer prompting across reasoning task types

datasets.name: Meta-analysis corpus
datasets.size: 4,642 papers screened, 516 with CoT keyword, 110 kept, 1,218 comparisons, 264 datasets
datasets.preprocessing: Excluded multimodal, CoT-fine-tuned, multi-pass (self-consistency, ToT), tool-augmented; best prompt per method; 0-100 scale only

datasets.name: 20 evaluation datasets
datasets.source: CommonsenseQA(7-shot), StrategyQA(6), SIQA, PIQA, Winogrande, ARC Easy, ARC Challenge, AGIEval LSAT(3), BiGGen Bench, MMLU(5), MMLU Pro(5), BBH, MuSR(1), GPQA(3), MuSiQue, GSM8K(8), GSM8K-Hard(8), FOLIO(4), ContextHub(3), MATH(4)
datasets.preprocessing: BiGGen: questions that say 'Think step-by-step' removed; ContextHub levels 1 and 2 only; MuSiQue judged by GPT-4o

models.name: Llama 2 7B Chat, Mistral 7B Instruct v0.3, Llama 3.1 8B/70B Instruct, Gemma 2 9B It, Phi-3 Small 8k, Qwen 2 7B/72B Instruct
models.context: Llama 2 and Gemma 4k (vLLM limit), Mistral 8k, Llama 3.1 128k, Qwen 131k

models.name: GPT-4o Mini (2024-07-18), GPT-4o (2024-08-06), Gemini 1.5 Flash/Pro, Claude 3 Haiku, Claude 3.5 Sonnet (20240620)

inference.decoding: greedy on all models (vLLM for open models)
inference.samples: one greedy run per model-dataset-prompt; no seeds stated
inference.prompting: zero-shot direct, zero-shot CoT (Kojima-style, 'Let's think step by step' in assistant turn where possible), few-shot direct, few-shot CoT (Wei-style); prompts mostly from Llama 3.1 evals; closed models that cannot prefix assistant turns use different prompts

parameters.plan_settings: Few-shot direct, few-shot CoT, Plan+Direct Solver, Plan+CoT Solver, Plan+Tool Solver (PAL Python interpreter for GSM8K; SatLM with Z3 for FOLIO and ContextHub); prompts from Ye et al. 2023
parameters.unparseable handling: random guess for multiple choice FOLIO/ContextHub, incorrect for GSM8K
parameters.equals_classifier: item has '=' in question or generated response

other.hardware: mostly 8 A40s or 4 Quadro RTX 8000s; others via API
other.max_tokens and sampling parameters: released on Huggingface, not in paper

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: Percent correct after answer extraction; BiGGen reports share of responses scoring >=4 from LLM judge

eval.protocol: Paired bootstrap with Bonferroni for knowledge/soft/commonsense datasets; unparseable rates reported (<=15% zero-shot, <10% for formal reasoning except tool)

availability.data: Prompts, outputs and sampling params on Huggingface (TAUR-Lab collection); meta-analysis paper list released

prompts.text: Solve the following math problem efficiently and clearly: - For simple problems (2 steps or fewer): Provide a concise solution with minimal explanation. - For complex problems (3 steps or more): Use this step-by-step format: ## Step 1: [Concise description] [Brief explanation and calculations] ## Step 2: ... Regardless of the approach, always conclude with: Therefore, the final answer is: $\boxed{answer}$. I hope it is correct.

Explain your reasoning step-by-step for each question before answering. Give your final answer in the format "The answer is therefore <A, B, C, D, E>". Failure to comply with the answer formatting will result in no credit. ... Let's think step by step.

prompts.purpose: CommonsenseQA zero-shot direct answer system prompt
prompts.text: You are a helpful AI assistant that will answer reasoning questions. You will always say at the end "Answer: <Your Answer Letter Choice>". You must only pick one answer and you must end your response with "Answer: <Your Answer Letter Choice>" everytime!

results.claim: Meta-analysis covers 110 papers and 1,218 experimental comparisons from ICLR 2024, EACL 2024 and NAACL 2024 (incl. Findings and Workshop), screened from 4,642 papers.
results.setup: Papers with >=2 mentions of CoT (516), manually filtered to CoT vs direct on the same model and dataset, 0-100 scale, best prompt each
results.quote:
A total of 110 papers were found that matched our criteria with 1,218 experimental com-
parisons.
results.note: Appendix A: 35 papers from ICLR and 75 from NAACL and EACL, covering 264 datasets; 516 papers after keyword filter.

results.claim: In the literature, CoT gains are largest for symbolic reasoning, then math, then logical reasoning.
Literature: top-3 categories average 56.9 with CoT vs 45.5 without.
results.quote:
Average perfor-
mance on these top three tasks with CoT was 56.9, whereas performance without CoT was 45.5.

results.claim: Literature: for all other categories CoT gives only 56.8 vs 56.1 direct.
results.quote: For other categories, the average performance with CoT was 56.8, compared to 56.1 without CoT.

results.claim: Own experiments: 20 datasets, 14 models, zero-shot and few-shot, greedy decoding via vLLM for open models.
results.setup: Models 7B to 72B open (Llama 2 7B to Llama 3.1 70B, Qwen 2 72B) plus closed models (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro etc.)
results.quote:
ran our own evaluations of
20 datasets across 14 models
results.note: Table 3 lists 12 models (no Qwen), Table 5 lists 14 and Table 6 has 14 rows; text says 14.

results.table: Table 6, row Average, columns Mathematical DA % and CoT %

results.table: Table 6, row Average, columns Symbolic DA % and CoT %

results.table: Table 6, row Average, columns Commonsense DA % and CoT %

results.table: Table 6, row Average, columns Knowledge and Soft

results.claim: On MMLU, as much as 95% of CoT gain comes from questions or outputs containing '='.
results.setup: MMLU, per model; the '=' feature classifies math-related items
results.quote:
As
much as 95% of the total performance gain from CoT on MMLU is attributed to questions
containing “=” in the question or generated output.
results.note: Abstract says: 'directly generating the answer without CoT leads to almost identical accuracy as CoT unless the question or model’s response contains an equals sign'. Table 18 max for a model with partial gain is 94.0% (Llama 3.1 70b); Qwen 2 7b shows 100.0% because the without-= delta is negative.

results.claim: MATH and GSM8K show gains as large as 41.6% and 66.9% from zero-shot CoT.
results.quote:
MATH and GSM8K show gains as large as 41.6%
and 66.9%, respectively.

results.table: Table 20, GSM8K rows CoT and Plan + Tool Solver, column Llama 3.1 70b Acc.
results.note: Tool solver does NOT beat CoT on plain GSM8K for this model; also Direct 39.1, Plan+CoT 94.7, Plan+Direct 42.2.

results.claim: GSM8K few-shot, GPT-4o Mini: CoT 94.2 vs Plan + Tool Solver 90.5.
results.table: Table 20, GSM8K rows CoT and Plan + Tool Solver, column GPT-4o Mini Acc.
results.note: Tool solver also below CoT here; direct 32.8, Plan+CoT 92.0.

results.claim: GSM8K-Hard few-shot, Llama 3.1 70B: CoT 47.8 vs Plan + Tool Solver 68.0.
results.table: Table 20, GSM8K-Hard rows CoT and Plan + Tool Solver, column Llama 3.1 70b Acc.

results.claim: GSM8K-Hard few-shot, GPT-4o Mini: CoT 52.2 vs Plan + Tool Solver 70.4.
results.table: Table 20, GSM8K-Hard rows CoT and Plan + Tool Solver, column GPT-4o Mini Acc.

results.claim: CoT is characterised as a poor but universal approximation to symbolic solvers.
results.setup: Sec 5 conclusion from plan/execute comparison on GSM8K, GSM8K-Hard, ContextHub, FOLIO
results.quote:
CoT appears to be a poor (but universal) approximation to
such solvers.

results.claim: Only 32% (59) of benefiting dataset-model pairs in Knowledge/Soft/Commonsense categories are significant after Bonferroni; 26 of those on MMLU and MMLU Pro.
results.setup: Paired bootstrap, 13 datasets x 14 models, p threshold 0.00027
results.quote:
About
32% (59) of the datasets that show a benefit in these three reasoning categories were considered
significant.

results.claim: Prompt wording matters little: four zero-shot CoT prompts on Llama 3.1 8B across 7 datasets vary little on average.
results.quote: There is very little variation between the CoT prompts on average.

results.claim: Few-shot CoT does not change which datasets benefit, only MuSR Team Allocation starts to improve.
results.quote:
Only one dataset, MuSR Team Allocation, starts to improve with
few-shot

results.claim: Direct-answer prompts give the answer within the first 60 characters; unparseable rates at or below 15%.
results.setup: Answer-span index, all models and datasets
results.quote:
direct answer prompts all return an answer within

limits: Long-horizon planning is not covered except via BiGGen Bench (Sec 6, App I.1).
Dataset contamination is unknown; mitigated by scale range, GSM8K-Hard, recent datasets, 2023 papers in the meta-analysis (App I.2).
Only single-prompt CoT; multi-call methods (self-consistency, ToT, debate), CoT-fine-tuned models and multimodal models are excluded.
Authors say a fair comparison would match compute (e.g. ensembling), so small CoT gains in the literature are not a win for CoT.
Models are mid-2024 instruction-tuned; dedicated reasoning models trained with RL are not studied (dated).
Why CoT does not help non-symbolic tasks is left open: pretraining limits vs missing modes of deliberation.
BiGGen lack of gain: 'Future work is needed to prove this.'
